prompt:
A hovercraft travels over a frozen lake with an initial velocity of v1 = 24.0 m s^-1 due east. After negotiating a turn over a time interval of 5.00 s, its velocity is v2 = 18.0 m s^-1 due north.

(a) State the vector operation used to determine the change in velocity delta v. [1]
(b) Calculate the magnitude of the change in velocity delta v. [1]
(c) Determine the direction of delta v, stating the angle with respect to north. [1]
(d) Calculate the magnitude of the average acceleration of the hovercraft during the turn. [1]

answer.text:
(a) delta v = v2 - v1 = v2 + (-v1).
(b) |delta v| = sqrt(18.0^2 + 24.0^2) = sqrt(324 + 576) = sqrt(900) = 30.0 m s^-1.
(c) theta = arctan(24.0 / 18.0) = arctan(1.333) = 53.1 degrees west of north.
(d) a = |delta v| / delta t = 30.0 m s^-1 / 5.00 s = 6.00 m s^-2.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Vector operation for change in velocity

mark_scheme: Part (a) [1 mark]: delta v = v2 - v1 OR v2 + (-v1) / reverse v1 and add to v2.
Part (c) [1 mark]: 53.1 degrees west of north (or 36.9 degrees north of west).
hints: Change in velocity is final velocity minus initial velocity.
Reverse the initial east velocity to get a west vector (-v1 = 24.0 m s^-1 west).
Combine the north and west vectors using Pythagoras.
Acceleration is delta v divided by delta t.
solution:
(a) delta v = v2 - v1 = v2 + (-v1).
(b) |delta v| = sqrt(18.0^2 + 24.0^2) = 30.0 m s^-1.
(c) tan(theta) = 24.0 / 18.0 = 1.333, so theta = 53.1 degrees west of north.
(d) a = 30.0 / 5.00 = 6.00 m s^-2.
